items.reason: The commit the item quotes predates the promotion: ci.yml's `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` are already blocking (no continue-on-error) and .githooks/pre-commit already runs cargo fmt --all -- --check over the author's staged .rs files, so the two explore questions were answered by reading, not by writing; the real residual hole was that nothing bound .ai/manifest.yaml's controls.ciHardPass — the machine-readable claim about what stops a merge — to the workflow's continue-on-error, so demoting fmt to advisory and flipping CONTRIBUTING's Blocking column in one commit passed every existing guard. crates/core/tests/blocking_gate_guard.rs now fails `cargo test --workspace` (itself a blocking CI job) when a ciHardPass capability maps to a missing/advisory job, when a ciAdvisory one maps to a blocking job, or when the mapped job stops running the manifest's command verbatim (fmt, clippy, workspace test, sqlite conformance, chart policy, gitleaks, rust SDK); it carries its own seeded-failure test. NOT closed, and named as such in CONTRIBUTING.md and in the test's header: whether those check names are marked *required* in GitHub branch protection is repository settings, not tree state, and no test here can read it.

Needs network: pinning the 34 Action refs means asking GitHub what each floating tag points at right now, and a guessed SHA breaks a workflow rather than pinning it — so all 34 stay unpinned and the next scan will still see that. The other half was done: release.yml and docker.yml are now `contents: read` workflow-wide, with `contents: write` (release assets, signature bundles) and `packages: write` (GHCR push) granted only to the jobs that use them, so the token beside cargo build's build scripts and proc macros can no longer publish or rewrite anything; soak.yml and ci.yml were already read-only. Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem is already configured and maintains SHA pins once introduced, so the burn-down is one-time — the exact `gh api` procedure is recorded in .github/dependabot.yml for whoever has a network.

Needs write access to .claude/CLAUDE.md, which this harness refuses as a sensitive path (second Ascent session to hit this — the pointer body was written and rejected, not skipped for effort). The npm scaffold is therefore still there and the two files still disagree. What could be done around it was: AGENTS.md now gives the other tool ecosystems the same pointer to the canonical CLAUDE.md and restates no command; crates/core/tests/guidance_guard.rs fails `cargo test --workspace` if a declared projection is missing, if a projection that is NOT in staleProjections carries a command line or stops naming the canonical file, or if a stale projection is not warned about in the canonical document — so removing .claude/CLAUDE.md from staleProjections without actually rewriting it turns the suite red, and no new guidance file can quietly become a second answer. The one-line human fix is recorded in .ai/manifest.yaml and CLAUDE.md.

lessons: The .claude/ write refusal is now a confirmed, repeatable property of this harness, not a one-off: two cycles have each burned an item on it. Any recommendation whose only fix is editing a file under .claude/ should be routed to a human at dispatch time rather than dispatched to an agent — or the canonical-guidance pointer should be expected to live somewhere writable (.ai/manifest.yaml and a root AGENTS.md both work).

In this repository a process gap is closed with a guard test, not a document: crates/core/tests/{manifest_guard,gate_table_guard,chart_policy_guard,blocking_gate_guard,guidance_guard}.rs each fail `cargo test --workspace` when a projection drifts from its authority, and each carries a seeded-failure test proving the parser can still go red. When adding one, check which authority already owns the fact — .ai/manifest.yaml for commands, .github/workflows/ci.yml for what blocks — and bind to that rather than introducing a fourth surface.

Scan items here are frequently stale in the safe direction: the 'formatting gate isn't blocking' evidence was a commit message from before the gate was promoted, and the 'no pre-commit hook' finding missed .githooks/pre-commit because it is a native git hook rather than a .pre-commit-config.yaml. Read the workflow and the hooks before writing anything — the real gap is usually one notch deeper (here: nothing bound the manifest's blocking claim to the workflow) and adding the tool the detector expected would have been pure noise.

A no-shell worktree cannot run rustfmt, so new Rust files are written blind against a blocking `cargo fmt --check`. Formatting-fragile constructs are worth avoiding on purpose: multi-line assert!/assert_eq! calls that would fit on one line get collapsed by rustfmt, and long method chains get rewrapped. Bind the argument to a `let` and keep lines well under 100 so there is only one formatting a reasonable rustfmt could produce.
